summary.tldr: Creates a 15-week EI benefit for adoptive and surrogacy parents, and extends adoption leave under the Canada Labour Code.
what_it_does: Creates a new 15-week Employment Insurance attachment benefit for people caring for a child placed with them for adoption, including a child surrendered by a surrogate mother under provincial surrogacy law.
Extends the benefit period when the child is in hospital, lets the weeks be shared between eligible claimants for the same child, and caps each claimant at 15 weeks.
Changes waiting-period rules so a parent who shares claims for the same child can sometimes skip or defer the waiting period.
Applies the same 15-week adoption benefit rules to self-employed people, and adds surrogacy to the adoption definition for that part of the Employment Insurance Act.
Extends Canada Labour Code adoption leave to up to 80 weeks, and counts children surrendered by a surrogate mother as children in the employee’s care for adoption.
who_it_affects: Employers covered by the Canada Labour Code
summary.background: This bill amends the Employment Insurance Act and the Canada Labour Code. The bill’s summary says it adds a new special benefit called an attachment benefit.
